plan.title: DBMS Examination Preparation
plan.original_input: Prepare for my DBMS examination covering SQL, normalization and transactions.
plan.description: A step-by-step low-capacity study plan covering SQL queries, database normalization, and transaction management for a DBMS exam.

steps.title: Review Syllabus and Outline Topics
steps.reason: Having a clear checklist ensures no major DBMS concepts are missed during study sessions.
steps.instruction: List out the specific sub-topics under SQL, normalization, and transactions that your exam will cover.

steps.title: Gather Study Materials
steps.reason: Centralizing all your resources saves time and keeps you focused.
steps.instruction: Collect your lecture notes, textbook chapters, and previous assignment solutions related to SQL, normalization, and transactions.
research_suggestions: DBMS lecture notes SQL normalization transactions

steps.title: Review SQL Basics and Joins
steps.reason: SQL queries form the practical foundation of DBMS exams and require a solid conceptual refresher.
steps.instruction: Read through your notes on basic SELECT statements, filtering, grouping, and various types of SQL joins.

steps.title: Practice Writing SQL Queries
steps.reason: Active practice solidifies query syntax and logic much better than passive reading.
steps.instruction: Write out solutions to three practice SQL problems involving multi-table joins and aggregate functions.

steps.title: Review Subqueries and Views
steps.reason: Complex SQL questions on exams frequently test nested logic and views.
steps.instruction: Go over your notes regarding subqueries, nested queries, and creating database views.

steps.title: Understand Functional Dependencies
steps.reason: Attribute closures are the mandatory first step for solving normalization problems.
steps.instruction: Review the definition of functional dependency and how to compute attribute closures.

steps.title: Study 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF
steps.reason: Normal forms are heavily tested theoretical concepts in every DBMS exam.
steps.instruction: Read through the definitions and rules for the first three normal forms with examples.

steps.title: Study BCNF and Normalization Practice
steps.reason: BCNF decomposition is a frequent advanced question type on database exams.
steps.instruction: Review Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) and work through one normalization decomposition problem.

steps.title: Review ACID Properties
steps.reason: ACID properties are fundamental guarantees expected in every transaction management question.
steps.instruction: Write down definitions and examples for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.
research_suggestions: ACID properties in DBMS exam questions

steps.title: Study Concurrency Control and Locking
steps.reason: Concurrency control ensures data integrity and is a core transaction exam topic.
steps.instruction: Review transaction schedules, serializability, and two-phase locking (2PL) protocols.

steps.title: Review Recovery Systems and Logs
steps.reason: Recovery mechanisms complete the transaction management portion of the syllabus.
steps.instruction: Read your notes on failure classification, log-based recovery, and check-pointing.

steps.title: Complete a Full Practice Exam
steps.reason: Simulating exam conditions tests your recall and time management across all three topic areas.
steps.instruction: Attempt a past paper or mixed problem set covering SQL, normalization, and transactions under timed conditions.
research_suggestions: DBMS past exam papers with solutions
